texts.preamble: Da vs Rajender Prasad on 9 February, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Abhishek Kumar Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate-01 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi District: New Delhi Ct Cases 1998/2023 Da Vs. Rajender Prasad Judgment
texts.facts: Initially, after conclusion of the trial, accused was convicted by the then Ld. ACMM vide order dated 06.02.2014 under section 16(1) (a) of the PFA act read with section 7 of the PFA act, for violation of rule 29 and was accordingly sentenced. 3. Thereafter, the accused had challenged the order of conviction and sentenece before the appellate court. . Furthermore, none of the parties requested or filed any application for adducing any additional evidence. Page No. 5 of 11 for violation of Rule 23 r/w Ruie 29 of PFA Rules 1955, punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w Section 7 of the Act. 13. After filing of the complaint, the accused was summoned vide order dated 17.07.2009. Upon entering appearance, accused Rajender Prasad who also represents accused no. 2 i.e. M/s NU Look Pvt. Ltd., moved an application under Section 13(2) of PFA Act to get the second counterpart of the sample analysed from Central Food Laboratory. Consequently, second counterpart of the sample as per the choice of the accused was sent to the Director, CFL (Pune) for its analysis vide order dated 30.07.2009. The Director, CFL after analysing the sample opined vide its Certificate dated 18.08.2009 that "sample contains Total Soluble Solids less than 10.0%, Synthetic food colour i.e. Tartrazine more than 100.00 ppm & hence does not conform to the standards of Fruit Juice as per P.F.A. Rules 1955 as per tests performed." 14. Thereafter, matter proceeded for the recording of the pre-charge evidence and the prosecution had examined Food Inspector Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW-1 and pre charge evidence was closed vide order dated 20.10.2009. The accused did not cross examine the witness despite opportunity. 15. Accordingly, vide order dated 15.12.2009, charge for the violation of provision of Section 2 (i-a) (a) (j) & (m) of PFA Act 1954, ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Page No. 6 of 11 Rule 23 r/w Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules 1955, punishable U/s 16 (1A) r/w section 7 of the Act was framed against the accused, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Then, the matter was kept for post-charge evidence. 16. During post charge evidence, the prosecution had examined three witnesses including Food Inspector Suniti Kumar Gupta as PW- 1, SDM / LHA, Sh. M.S. Vats as PW-2 and Field Assistant Ashok Kumar as PW-3. Thereafter, post charge evidence was closed vide order dated 31.03.2012. The accused availed the opportunity to duly cross examine all the witnesses. 17. Then, the statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 CrPC and he did not lead any defence evidence despite opportunity being afforded. Thereafter, the final arguments were heard and accused was convicted.
